Your home's up $150,000? Costs can eat most of it.
The Case-Shiller US home price index rose about 82% from 2016 to 2025.
Our example: paid $300,000 in 2016, worth $450,000 in 2026. Selling at 6% costs $27,000; a $240,000 loan at 3.65% charges about $78,600 interest in 10 years. About $44,400 of the gain left (our math), before taxes, insurance and repairs.
And CPI rose 34% from 2016 to 2025.
Sources: S&P Case-Shiller and BLS via FRED, Freddie Mac, Redfin.
Owners also skip rent, which this doesn't count.
News and education, not financial advice.
